assets.feature: A faint irregular-edged rectangle where a small adhesive label was peeled away near ONE rear corner, and TWO short unequal handling scratches on the top rim close to only ONE front handle. Keep the broad lid almost clean; no mirrored scuffs, no giant gray scratch field. The residue rectangle should read as a subdued local change of sheen, not a readable label.

A faint incomplete cup/jar ring in the EMPTY right-hand portion of the wooden top, and a lightly thumb-softened corner on only the nearest archive carton. Keep carton positions and grain. The mark implies someone briefly set a cup there, not a dirty warehouse surface. No identical ring on every object.

Near the existing tray, add a small irregular cluster of THREE subdued brownish dry droplets of unequal size and one short fine drag mark leading away from the tray edge. The rest of the off-white worktop remains clean and usable. Change no construction or tray contents; this is an isolated trace of a task, not generalized damage.

Replace exactly ONE ventilation-cover screw with a slightly brighter hex-head fastener and washer, visibly different from the remaining original screws. Near the round access cap add a small uneven brush-touch-up patch in almost matching steel-gray paint. The patch is subtle but locally legible, no long scratched lines all over the roof, no changed vents.

Give only ONE existing clamp a slightly warmer/darker replacement finish and add a short localized rub beside that clamp, as if it was tightened with a tool. Keep the remaining tube length quieter. Preserve the exact straight axis, outer diameter, both flat terminal ports, and all connection geometry. Do not put a uniform distressed/noise texture over the pipe.

Add one narrow uneven repair/weld trace on a short section of the OUTSIDE curve and a small muted greasy thumb rub next to only one existing clamp. Preserve the exact bend radius, pipe diameter and straight terminal ends. No dents, sagging, kinked arc, general corrosion or chunky weld beads.

A small faded chalk maintenance stroke on ONE arm near the central junction, formed by two casual unequal strokes without readable letters, and a small wiped patch around it. Keep the other arms clean, exact T-junction and equal tube diameters unchanged. No decorative perfectly centered white logo or mirrored marks.

One of the two center clamp fasteners has been replaced by a slightly brighter hex head while the other remains the old round head. Add a small localized dark handling smudge next to the replaced fastener. Preserve the exact silhouette, width and both terminal stubs. No allover scuffing.

On one short section of the handwheel rim, remove just a little red paint where a palm commonly grips it, revealing muted dull metal; keep most of the wheel paint intact. Add a small greasy wipe close to its hub, no symmetrical abrasion. Preserve round coherent wheel, spokes, stem, pipe axis, diameter and terminal geometry.

The owner explicitly requests non-identical caster directions: turn the LOWER-LEFT swivel caster's actual wheel and fork about 55 degrees relative to the three remaining wheels while keeping its mounting point attached and all four wheels physically functional. Make this directional difference visible, not just rotate its highlights. Add a faint incomplete dried jar ring near one upper tray corner and only two short fine utensil drag scuffs nearby. The metal tray remains mostly empty and maintained. Do not bend the frame, mirror these marks, make every wheel crooked, or cover it with grime.
